::: {.result-banner}
Trained 300,000+ demand-forecasting models across a CPG portfolio to optimize trade promotions — delivering ~$2.4M in client savings, on pipelines processing 100M+ rows a day.
:::

## The problem

A CPG client planned trade promotions off forecasts that were too coarse to trust at the SKU × store level, so promo spend was routinely mis-sized. The business needed accurate, per-series demand forecasts across a very large portfolio — and needed them to refresh fast enough to plan against. ## The finding

```{python}
#| label: fig-hero
#| fig-cap: "Per-series forecast vs. actuals with prediction interval. Replace the synthetic series with a representative real backtest window."
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

rng = np.random.default_rng(11)
t = np.arange(60)
base = 100 + 18 * np.sin(t / 6)
actual = base + rng.normal(0, 5, 60)
actual[20:24] += 40          # a promotion spike
fc = base.copy(); fc[20:24] += 34
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.2))
ax.fill_between(t, fc - 10, fc + 10, color="#2563eb", alpha=0.12, label="80% interval")
ax.plot(t, actual, color="#8a909a", lw=1.6, label="actual")
ax.plot(t, fc, color="#2563eb", lw=2.6, label="forecast")
ax.axvspan(20, 23, color="#fde68a", alpha=0.4, label="promotion")
ax.set_xlabel("week"); ax.set_ylabel("units")
ax.legend(frameon=False, ncol=2)
for s in ["top", "right"]: ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["left"].set_color("#d5d5df"); ax.spines["bottom"].set_color("#d5d5df")
ax.grid(axis="y", color="#eef0f4", lw=1)
plt.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("hero.png", dpi=120, bbox_inches="tight", facecolor="white")
plt.show()
```

Getting the promotion weeks right (the yellow band) is where the savings came from — that's where a generic forecast fails and money is left on the table.

## Decisions and tradeoffs

Training a separate model per series (300k+ of them) was a deliberate choice over one global model: it captured per-SKU seasonality and promo response that a pooled model washed out, at the cost of a much heavier training and orchestration burden. I ran this on a distributed stack (PySpark / Databricks / Dask) so the whole portfolio could retrain on 100M+ rows a day.
